newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CAR DEALERS SEE RISING NEW CAR SALES 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CAR DEALERS SEE RISING NEW CAR SALES 1997-98.

text.p: Sales of new private cars in Finland will increase to 102,000 in 1997 from 95,000 forecast for this year, and rise further to 110,000 in 1998, the Information Centre of the Automobile Branch said in a statement on Wednesday.
"Car dealers expect the growth in automobile sales to continue in the next few years," the centre said, adding, however, that in general, dealers' sales growth expectations were "very moderate".
According to the car dealers' new forecast, "102,000 new private cars will be sold next year and 110,000 in 1998," the centre said.

Its survey among car dealers showed that "a clear majority" (68 percent) expected sales of new private cars to exceed 100,000 next year. The current forecast for 1996 sales of new private cars is 95,000.
One fifth of respondents expected sales of new private cars to remain below 100,000 next year while 12 percent forecast sales to exceed 105,000.

Asked about the outlook for 1998, 72 percent of the car dealers participating in the centre's survey said sales of new private cars would be between 105,000 and 115,000, 15 percent forecast sales below 105,000 and 13 percent saw sales in excess of 115,000.
New private car registrations in Finland peaked at nearly 180,000 in 1988-89, but fell sharply, to below 60,000 in 1993 as the Finnish economy plunged into recession.
